radio.title: Field radio channel
radio.not_chosen: not chosen yet: the recommended one applies
radio.low_power_warning: This channel allows only 25 mW and about a tenth of the recommended channel's airtime: less range, and with many boxes their transmissions may run out of allowed time.
radio.first_setup: Before the first game, choose the field's radio channel. Until then it is {channel} MHz, the recommended one.
radio.why_1: It is the centre of 869.4–869.65 MHz, the only part of the European 868 MHz band where a device may transmit up to 10% of the time at up to 500 mW (ERP). Everywhere else in 868–870 MHz the rules allow 1% of the time (0.1% on 868.7–869.2 MHz) at 25 mW: about a tenth of the airtime, and much less range.
radio.why_2: 868.1, 868.3 and 868.5 MHz are the channels every LoRaWAN device in Europe starts on, so they are often busy.
radio.why_3: The recommended channel is shared: LoRaWAN gateways send some of their replies on 869.525 MHz, and Meshtastic's European default is the same frequency. Their packets are not mistaken for the game's (the game's are encrypted and use another sync word), but every transmission nearby uses the same airtime. If such users are near the field, a scan shows whether another channel is quieter.
radio.locked_game: A game is live: end it to change the channel.
radio.default_hint: {channel} MHz: the most airtime and power European rules allow (see above).
radio.scan_hint: The USB modem listens to each candidate channel, about {seconds} s in all, without transmitting, and lists them quietest first. Nothing changes until you accept.

unavailable.no_modem: No USB modem is configured, so there is no radio to measure the noise with. The channel stays as it is.
unavailable.modem_down: The USB modem is not connected; the scan needs it.
unavailable.no_radio: The USB modem has no radio chip, so it cannot measure the noise.
unavailable.old_firmware: The USB modem's firmware cannot measure noise: update it.

suggest.quiet_full_power: Suggested: {channel} MHz, the quietest full-power channel ({limits}).
suggest.quietest: Suggested: {channel} MHz, the quietest channel ({limits}). The 500 mW channels were noisier.
suggest.quietest_but_noisy: Every channel is noisy. The least noisy is {channel} MHz ({limits}).

radio.results_caption: Quietest first. Quiet: 90% of the readings at {threshold} dBm or lower, and little LoRa activity.
radio.random_hint: Draws one of the candidate channels. It will usually be a 1%, 25 mW channel; only 869.475, 869.525 and 869.575 MHz give 10% and 500 mW.
radio.low_airtime_warning: 0.1% of the time: about 3.6 s of transmission per hour for each device, too little for a game.
radio.read_only: Only the organisers can change the channel.

checkin.title: Field check-in
checkin.intro: Players scan the field's poster with the app, check in and declare the replicas they will use in this game. Names are shown only here and in the marshals' view.
checkin.empty: Nobody has checked in to this game yet.
checkin.name: Name
checkin.manual_hint: For players without the app: the controller makes their id, which can be written to a player tag.
checkin.valid_day: A pass counts for the rest of the day at this field.
checkin.valid_game: Every game asks for a new chronograph.
checkin.unregistered: not registered at the field yet
checkin.confirm_staff: by the GM or a marshal
checkin.federation_note: The federation number is never verified automatically: “required” only stops the form being sent without it. Tick “card seen” once you have seen the card.
checkin.poster_intro: Print it once and put it up in the check-in area: it serves every game at the field. It holds no key and no password.
checkin.poster_urls: The controller's https addresses (one per line)
checkin.no_game: No game is live: create one to open check-in. The poster can be printed now.

poster.title: Check-in poster
poster.login: Open the console with the GM token first.
poster.no_text: The poster cannot be made yet.
poster.qr_label: QR code for checking in at the field
poster.intro: Print this page on A4. The code holds no secrets: it can stay in plain view.
poster.wifi_label: QR code for the Wi-Fi network
poster.wifi_note: The password is used only to draw the Wi-Fi code: it is neither kept nor sent.

branding.title: Field branding
branding.intro: How players see this field: its name, logo, wallpaper and colour, in the app, on the scoreboard, on the check-in poster and in this console. Anyone on the field's network can see them; they hold no personal data.
branding.field_name_hint: Also printed on the check-in poster.
branding.accent_hint: On the app's main buttons and this console's header.
branding.limits: PNG, JPEG or WebP (no SVG). Logo up to 1 MB and 2048 px a side, wallpaper up to 4 MB and 4096 px a side. Metadata such as the camera or where a photo was taken is removed.
branding.rights: Upload only images you have the right to use (your field's or club's own, or with the owner's permission): you are responsible for them.
branding.bad_type: The image must be PNG, JPEG or WebP.
branding.read_only: Only the GM can change the field's branding.

teams.title: Saved teams
teams.intro: Teams that come back: a name and a crest to pick when you create a game. The colour stays the team's colour on the boxes and buttons.
teams.name: Team name
teams.crest_limits: PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 512 KB and 1024 px a side.
teams.for_game_hint: Optional: a name and a crest for each team colour, shown to players, on the scoreboard and on Android props. The boxes keep showing the colour.
